answer: A tide of new identities hits the market: each newcomer must pass a random peer audit before trading. Auditors are drawn by lottery; the newcomer stakes 20 credits and an ivory-sealed work record. The audit samples a plume of recent transactions against on-chain history: pass returns the stake plus 5 credits, fail burns it. Forging 100 identities burns 2,000 credits, while an honest agent pays once and earns audit fees, so bulk forgery drowns.
